CORE_EVIDENCE_FILE_BEGIN
CORE_EVIDENCE_STATUS: USED
CORE_SOURCE_BASIS: Core Radiology, Second Edition, `junzi-shi-core-radiology-a-visual-approach-to.pdf`; Genitourinary Imaging, “Adnexal torsion,” GU p. 315.
CORE_FACTS_USED:

* Adnexal torsion results from twisting of the ovarian vascular pedicle with potential vascular compromise.
* Torsion occurs mainly in reproductive-age women and commonly occurs in pregnancy.
* A lead-point adnexal mass predisposes to torsion; Core emphasizes ovarian dermoid.
* Dual ovarian arterial supply explains why color Doppler flow may remain detectable despite torsion.
* Classic ultrasound pattern includes an enlarged edematous ovary, abnormal Doppler findings, and free fluid.
* Ovary >4 cm, unusual ovarian position, peripheral follicles, and variable Doppler findings are key imaging clues.
* Lack of flow is not required and, when present, usually indicates necrosis or infarction.
* Normal/intermittent flow and absent or reversed arterial diastolic flow may occur.
* CT and MRI share the core morphology of ovarian enlargement and peripheral follicles from central hemorrhage/edema.
* Twisting of the ovarian pedicle is uncommon to visualize but pathognomonic when identified.
CORE_DERIVED_CARDS:
* PRIMARY UNKNOWN recognition cards using ovarian enlargement, abnormal position, peripheral follicles, variable Doppler, and twisted-pedicle logic.
* Differential Drill cards distinguishing torsion from common adnexal mimics.
* Definition card: “Define adnexal torsion.”
* Mechanism cards explaining edema/peripheral follicles, preserved arterial flow, vascular failure, and twisted-pedicle specificity.
* Boards Trap card addressing preserved Doppler flow.
* Epidemiology High-Yield cards for reproductive-age predominance and pregnancy association.
* High-Yield cards covering >4 cm ovarian enlargement, Doppler pitfalls, ultrasound appearance, CT/MRI appearance, lead-point lesions, and twisted-pedicle specificity.
CORE_LIMITATIONS:
* Core p. 315 provides a concise board-level torsion section rather than the full RadPrimer/STATdx depth.
* More detailed venous-first physiology, viability indicators, isolated fallopian tube torsion, neonatal variants, CT frequency of pedicle visualization, >50 HU hemorrhage, and expanded MRI/lead-point details were derived from the supplied RadPrimer + STATdx master source rather than attributed to Core.
CORE_EVIDENCE_FILE_END
